summary: Enrollment-only prototype passes isolated attack tests; full production LMS integration remains blocked by permissive legacy rules and staff-profile access migration.

findings.issue: The isolated default-deny rules intentionally do not authorize the remaining LMS collections or staff profile queries. The legacy catch-all would bypass enrollment protections if retained.
findings.recommendation: Migrate unrelated collection policies and staff PII queries, then review and test one combined ruleset before production deployment.

findings.issue: No live issuer UID has been approved or bootstrapped. Existing editable profile roles cannot establish trusted authority.
findings.recommendation: Obtain explicit approval of the initial issuer UID and provision it only after client writes to issuer records are denied.

findings.issue: Unauthenticated capability lookups can consume Spark read quota even though the secret is high entropy and the returned data contains no PII.
findings.recommendation: Monitor quotas and abuse. A trusted rate-limited backend is required for stronger automated abuse protection.

attack_results.public_list_and_mixed_content: denied; only exact capability GET returns expiry
attack_results.query_compatibility: enrollment queries only; broader LMS rollout blocked
attack_results.counter_and_array_attacks: not applicable; no counters or array fields in enrollment schema
